newsitem.title: POLAND: Snapshot of Poland's National Investment Funds.
newsitem.headline: Snapshot of Poland's National Investment Funds.

text.p: Poland's 15 National Investment Funds (NFIs), comprising more than 500 companies privatised under the country's mass privatisation scheme, begin trading on the Warsaw Stock Exchange on Thursday.

Each fund gained strategic stakes in about 30 companies and small minority stakes in several hundred others and are managing their assets either directly or through international asset management consortia.
Following is a full list of all 15 funds with their brief descriptions:
* PIERWSZY NARODOWY FUNDUSZ INWESTYCYJNY SA (I NFI)
Managing firm: BRE/IB Austria consortium
Shareholders: Bank Rozwoju Eksportu SA (51 pct), Investmentbank Austria (49 pct).
Net Assets Q1 1997: 412 million zlotys
Net Profit Q1 1997: 5.5 million zlotys
The fund plans to invest in unlisted companies not included in the programme. In the near term it plans to buy two firms.
It wants to find strategic investors for 8-12 companies from its portfolio. It has one listed company: Lentex SA * II NARODOWY FUNDUSZ INWESTYCYJNY SA (II NFI)
Managing firm: none
Net Assets Q1 1997: 459.2 million zlotys
Net Profit Q1 1997: 5.0 million zlotys.

In the next five years the fund plans to evolve into a typical investment fund. Construction, chemical and electrical engineering companies dominate in its portfolio. The fund plans to float three or four firms this year.
* III NARODOWY FUNDUSZ INWESTYCYJNY SA (III NFI)
Managing firm: Trinity Management Sp z o.o.
Shareholders: Barclays de Zoete Wedd Int. Hldgs (33.3 pct), Pekao SA (33.3 pct), Company Assistance Limited (33.3 pct).
Net Assets Q1 1997): 345.5 million zlotys
Net Profit Q1 1997: 4.0 million zlotys

The leading firms in the fund's portfolio are active in the construction industry. This year the fund plans to find strategic investors for three or four companies. It is also considering investments in about 10 companies outside of the programme. The fund has one listed company PEPEES SA PEPWs.WA food firm and may float another one shortly.
* NARODOWY FUNDUSZ INWESTYCYJNY PROGRESS SA (IV NFI)
Managing firm: Raiffeisen Atkins Zarzadzanie Funduszami SA.

Shareholders: Raiffeisen Investment AG (26 pct), Raiffeisen Centrobank SA (25 pct), WS Atkins (25 pct), Idea Sp z o.o. (9.5 pct), WIL Consulting House Ltd Sp. z o.o. (9.5 pct), ADIN Sp. z o.o. (5 pct).
Net Assets Q1 1997: 404.5 million zlotys
Net Profit Q1 1997: 47.4 million zlotys
In the next few months Progress plans to increase capital of three leading companies in its portfolio by $10 million.

The fund mulls investments in about 10 companies outside of its portfolio. This year it plans to conclude three of them. Progress plans to float on the bourse one company in the second half of the year and place another one on the OTC market.
* V NARODOWY FUNDUSZ INWESTYCYJNY VICTORIA SA (V NFI).
Managing firm: Polskie Towarzystwo Prywatyzacyjne Kleinwort Benson Sp z o.o.
Shareholders: Kleinwort Benson Investment Overseas B.V. (50.1 pct), Polska Grupa Zarzadzania Funduszami Sp z o.o. (49.9 pct)
Net Assets Q1 1997: 329.7 million zlotys
Net Profit Q1 1997: 5.4 million zlotys

Victoria's strategy focuses on investments in small and medium non-public firms. It plans to list two or three firms out of its portfolion within the next two years. By the end of 1997 it plans to sell large stakes in three or four companies.
* VI NARODOWY FUNDUSZ INWESTYCYJNY MAGNA POLONIA SA (VI NFI)
Managing Firm: Chase Gemina Polska Sp. z o.o.
Shareholders: Chase Manhattan International Finance Ltd (51 pct), Wielkopolski Bank Kredytowy SA (29 pct), Nicom Consulting Ltd. (20 pct)
Net Assets Q1 1997: 327.8 million zlotys
Net Profit Q1 1997: 1.1 million zlotys

The fund plans to invest up to $10 million this year mainly in the companies from its portfolio. Magna Polonia does not plan any flotations this year and one or two in 1998. It has selected mainly automotive and chemical firms for its portfolio.
* VII NARODOWY FUNDUSZ INWESTYCYJNY IM. KAZIMIERZA WIELKIEGO
Managing Firm: Kazimierz Wielki Fund Management Co.
Shareholders: GICC Capital Corporation (33.33 pct), Lazard Freres et Cie (33.33 pct), Bank Gospodarstwa Krajowego SA (33.33 pct).
Net Assets Q1 1997: 378.4 million zlotys
Net Profit Q1 1997: 6.7 million zlotys

The fund plans to reduce the number of controlling stakes in its portfolio to about 20 from the current 34 within three years. The fund plans to hold on to about one third of companies in its portfolio which are in good financial health.

It also wants to focus on about 50 firms in which it holds small minority stakes. Kazimierz Wielki plans to list on the bourse two or three companies next year and mniejszociowe and to place six further on the OTC market.
* NARODOWY FUNDUSZ INWESTYCYJNY OCTAVA (VIII NFI)
Managing Firm: KP Konsorcjum Sp z o.o.
Shareholders: KP International Limited (60 pct), Bank Handlowy SA (20 pct), Paine Webber Inc. (20 pct).
Net Assets Q1 1997: 346.8 million zlotys
Net Profit Q1 1997: 7.8 million zlotys

The fund plans to reduce the number of so-called leading 33 percent stakes to 15-20 from more than 30 now and spin off hundreds of small minority stakes. No plans for listings this year. Octava said about 40 percent of companies in its portfolio show high growth potential and the fund wants to keep them for 3-5 years. It plans to finance its investments mainly internally.
* NARODOWY FUNDUSZ INWESTYCYJNY IM.E.KWIATKOWSKIEGO (IX NFI)
Managing Firm: none.
Net Assets Q1 1997: 369.7 million zlotys
Net Profit Q1 1997: 1.9 million zlotys

Kwiatkowski wants to become a venture-capital type closed-ended fund with 80-90 percent of assets held in long-term investments. Chemical and electrical engineering companies make up the biggest part of its portfolio. Listed companies: Izolacja SA and ZEW SA ZEWWs.WA.
* NARODOWY FUNDUSZ INWESTYCYJNY FOKSAL SA (X NFI)
Management Firm: Fidea Management SA
Shareholders: Banque Arjil Cie (49 pct), Agencja Rozwoju Przemyslu SA (22.93 pct), Warszawska Grupa Konsultingowa Sp. z o.o. (22.93 pct), Bank Inicjatyw Spoleczno-Ekonomicznych (5.14 pct)
Net Assets Q1 1997: 463.7 million zlotys
Net Profit Q1 1997: 9.9 million zlotys

Foksal focuses its activities on chemical, fire-proof materials, industrial construction and food processing industries. It plans to create a group of poultry processing companies. It plans to float next year three companies on the bourse and to place one firm on the regulated OTC market.
* XI NARODOWY FUNDUSZ INWESTYCYJNY (XI NFI)
Management Firm: none
Net Assets Q1 1997: 400.7 million zlotys
Net Profit Q1 1997: 26.9 million zlotys

By the end of 1999 the fund plans to reduce the share of leading 33-percent stakes in its portfolio to 31 percent from 55 percent. It expects to list on the bourse two companies this year and two on the OTC market. Its Viscoplast VISOs.WA is listed. It plans to inject a total of 33 million zlotys in eight companies this year and to seek strategic investors for further three.
* NARODOWY FUNDUSZ INWESTYCYJNY PIAST SA (XII NFI)
Managing Firm: Eurofund Management Polska Sp z o.o.
Shareholders: Camai International B.V. (75 pct), Polski Bank Inwestycyjny (25 pct).
Net Assets Q1 1997: 382.3 million zlotys
Net Profit Q1 1997: 353 million zlotys

The fund describes itself as a restructuring one. It focuses on chemical, textile and automotive industries. Piast plans to bring in strategic investors to three companies from its portfolio. It does not plan to float any firms this year. earlier this year it acquired 32.9 percent of Prochnik SA garment maker.
* NARODOWY FUNDUSZ INWESTYCYJNY FORTUNA SA (XIII NFI)
Managing Firm: Yamaichi Regent ABC Polska Sp. z o.o.
Shareholders: Yamaichi Regent Special Projekt Ltd (90 pct), ABC Consulting Sp. z o.o. (10 pct)
Net Assets Q1 1997: 477.6 million zlotys
Net Profit Q1 1997: 9.0 million zlotys

Fortuna describes itself as a restructuring-growth fund and plans to evolve into a typical investment fund. It plans to float five companies in 1997 and 1998. The fund is in talks with construction firms interested in forming joint ventures with the fund's construction firms or acquiring them.
* ZACHODNI NARODOWY FUNDUSZ INWESTYCYJNY (XIV NFI)
Managing Firm: International Westfund Limited
Shareholders: Bank Zachodni SA (33,67 pct), Central Europe Trust Company Ltd. (33 pct), Charterhouse Development Limited (22.22 pct), Credit Commercial de France (11.11 pct).
Net Assets Q1 1997): 374 million zlotys
Net Profit Q1 1997: 43.4 million zlotys

Zachodni plans to invest in non-public companies. It plans to float four companies this year and to find strategic investors for another four. Zachodni does not rule out selling smaller companies to their managements. It wants to step up its involvement in about 50 companies in which it holds small minority stakes and expects to up its stakes in about 15 of them.
* NARODOWY FUNDUSZ INWESTYCYJNY HETMAN SA (XV NFI)
Managing Firm: Creditanstalt SCG Fund Management SA.
Shareholders: Creditannstalt Investment Bank AG (49.625 pct), SCG St. Gallen Investment Holding AG (49.625 pct).
Net Assets Q1 1997: 401.3 million zlotys
Net Profit Q1 1997: 653.000 zlotys

The fund plans to hold on to most of the companies in its portfolio over a longer-term. Hetman is focused on minerals and food processing industries which account for 19 percent and 15 percent of its portfolio respectively.
It plans to list one company early in 1998. Its Grajewo is listed on the bourse's parallel market.
The fund plans to buy shares of companies outside of the NFI programme. The fund is in talks on a sale of five companies from its portfolio to strategic investors.
